cities.name: Madinah al-Munawwarah
cities.about: The city of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), where he lived after the Hijrah and where he is buried in his mosque. Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) and four of the Imams (a.s.) - Imam Hasan, Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq - are buried here too, the Imams in Jannat al-Baqi beside the mosque. Pilgrims also visit Hamzah (a.s.) and the martyrs at Uhud and pray in the mosques the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed in.
tips: Most pilgrims stay near the Prophet's Mosque and walk to it and to al-Baqi, which lies just east of its courtyard.
It is recommended to do ghusl on arriving in Madinah and before the ziyarat of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.); see [Etiquettes of Ziyarat](B3).

Local rules restrict some acts at graves: touching or kissing the grilles, praying facing a grave and reciting aloud in groups are usually stopped. Pilgrims recite the ziyarat quietly, standing at a respectful distance.
The city is most crowded in the weeks around Hajj (Dhul Qa'dah and Dhul Hijjah) and in Ramazan.
Men and women visit the Rawdah at separate times. Women cannot enter al-Baqi and recite the ziyarat of the Imams (a.s.) from outside its wall.

sites.name: Masjid al-Nabawi and the Tomb of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
sites.about: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) own mosque, which he built after the Hijrah; his tomb lies in his house at its south-eastern corner, under the Green Dome. The area between his tomb and his minbar is the Rawdah, which he called one of the gardens of Paradise, and a prayer in his mosque is narrated to equal a thousand elsewhere. The burial place of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) was kept hidden; by different narrations it is her house (now inside the mosque, beside the Prophet's chamber), the Rawdah, or al-Baqi, and scholars recommend visiting her in all three. See [Method of Ziyarat of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in Madinah](AP2).

ziyarat.note: At the door of the mosque, before entering.
Most scholars recite it from the Rawdah; visiting her in her house and at al-Baqi as well is better.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.): With the Longer Form

ziyarat.note: For 3 Jumada al-Akhirah, one of the narrated dates of her martyrdom.
After the ziyarat.

ziyarat.label: Farewell to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
ziyarat.note: Before leaving Madinah.

buried.name: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)
buried.arabicName: النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وآله
buried.note: The Seal of the Prophets, buried in his house, now the chamber under the Green Dome.

buried.name: Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.)
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) daughter, buried secretly at night; her house beside the Prophet's chamber and the Rawdah are two of the places where, by narration, her grave is said to be.

tips: Enter by Bab Jibril if you can, right foot first, and say Allahu Akbar a hundred times; then pray the two rak'at greeting of the mosque before going to the tomb.
Stand facing the tomb from the side of the Rawdah or the passage in front of the chamber; pilgrims recite quietly and keep moving with the crowd.
In the Rawdah and at the place of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) minbar, pray as much as you can and ask for your needs.

Pray also at the place of Lady Fatimah's (s.a.) house, which adjoins the Prophet's chamber, and recite her ziyarat there; and at the place of Jibril (maqam Jibril), under the old waterspout, say the short dua given in the method of ziyarat.

sites.name: Jannat al-Baqi
sites.about: The oldest cemetery of Madinah, beside the Prophet's Mosque, where four of the Imams (a.s.) are buried with many of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) family and companions. Their graves had domes until these were demolished in 1806 and again on 8 Shawwal 1344 AH (1926); today the graves are plain mounds of earth. By one narration al-Baqi is also the burial place of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.), and Bayt al-Ahzan, the place where she mourned her father, stood here south of the Imams' graves.

ziyarat.label: Greeting the Believers Buried Here
ziyarat.note: On entering the cemetery.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Ibrahim, Son of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
Ziyarat of Lady Fatimah bint Asad (s.a.)

ziyarat.note: Al-Baqi is one of the places where she is said to be buried.
After the ziyarat of the Imams (a.s.).

ziyarat.label: Farewell to the Four Imams (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: When leaving al-Baqi.

buried.name: Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.)
buried.note: The second Imam; the four Imams lie side by side near the gate, to the right as one enters.

buried.name: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.)
buried.arabicName: الإمام علي بن الحسين زين العابدين عليه السلام
buried.note: The fourth Imam, buried beside his uncle Imam Hasan (a.s.).

buried.name: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.)
buried.note: The fifth Imam, buried beside his father.

buried.name: Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.)
buried.note: The sixth Imam, buried beside his father.

buried.name: Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) uncle, buried with the four Imams (a.s.) under the same former dome.

buried.name: Lady Fatimah bint Asad (s.a.)
buried.note: Mother of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), who raised the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The exact spot of her grave is not marked today: some place it at the far (north-eastern) end of the cemetery, others beside the Imams (a.s.).

buried.name: Lady Umm al-Baneen (s.a.)
buried.note: Wife of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and mother of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.); by tradition buried beside the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) aunts. The exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Ibrahim, Son of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) son by Mariyah, who died as an infant and was buried here at his father's command. His grave had a dome until 1926; the exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Daughters of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
buried.note: Zainab, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum, by the common account. The exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Wives of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
buried.note: Most of his wives, among them Umm Salamah; Lady Khadijah (s.a.) is buried in Makkah. The exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Aqil ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Ja'far
buried.arabicName: عقيل بن أبي طالب وعبد الله بن جعفر
buried.note: Amir al-Mu'minin's (a.s.) brother, and his nephew Abdullah son of Ja'far al-Tayyar, husband of Lady Zainab (s.a.); buried side by side. The exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Safiyyah and Atikah, Aunts of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
buried.note: Daughters of Abd al-Muttalib. Ibn Battuta found Safiyyah's grave the first on the left inside the old gate; the exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Ismail ibn Ja'far al-Sadiq
buried.note: Eldest son of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), who died in his father's lifetime. The exact spot is not marked today.

buried.name: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) foster mother. The exact spot is not marked today.

tips: Only men can enter, at set times of the day; women recite the ziyarat from outside the wall, facing the Imams' graves.
The Imams' (a.s.) graves are close to the main gate on the western side, to the right as you enter; stand facing the graves with your back to the qiblah, as the narration teaches.
Touching graves, praying beside them and reciting aloud are not allowed by the cemetery's guards; recite quietly and pray the ziyarat prayer afterwards in the Prophet's Mosque.
On 8 Shawwal, the anniversary of the demolition, many pilgrims and believers remember al-Baqi.

sites.name: Uhud: Tomb of Hamzah (a.s.) and the Martyrs
sites.about: At the foot of Mount Uhud, north of the city, lie the Muslims killed in the Battle of Uhud in Shawwal 3 AH, among them the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) uncle Hamzah, the Master of Martyrs of his time. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is narrated to have said that whoever visits his tomb and not his uncle Hamzah's has deserted him. Opposite the graves is the small hill of the archers (Jabal al-Rumat), where the battle turned.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Hamzah (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: At his tomb.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of the Martyrs of Uhud
Greeting the Believers Buried Here
ziyarat.note: On arriving at the graves.

buried.name: Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (a.s.)
buried.arabicName: حمزة بن عبد المطلب سيد الشهداء
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) uncle and early defender, martyred at Uhud.

buried.name: The Martyrs of Uhud
buried.note: About seventy Muslims killed in the battle, buried around Hamzah (a.s.).

tips: The graves are inside a walled enclosure; pilgrims recite the ziyarat from the railing outside.
After the ziyarat of Hamzah (a.s.) it is recommended to pray two rak'at, and after the ziyarat of the martyrs to recite Surah al-Qadr as many times as you can.

sites.name: Masjid Quba
sites.about: The first mosque of Islam, built by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) on his arrival from Makkah, where he waited for Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to join him; the Quran calls it the mosque founded on piety (9:108). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is narrated to have said that two rak'at prayed in it equal an Umrah, and Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) said to begin with it when visiting the mosques around Madinah.
tips: Pray the two rak'at greeting of the mosque and as many prayers as you can; making wudu before setting out is recommended.
Nearby are the sites of Mashrabat Umm Ibrahim, the house of Mariyah where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to pray, and Masjid al-Fadikh (Masjid al-Shams), where pilgrims also pray two rak'at.

sites.name: Masjid al-Fath (Masjid al-Ahzab)
sites.about: A small mosque on the slope of Mount Sal' where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed for victory during the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq or al-Ahzab), in which Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) killed Amr ibn Abd Wudd. Below it stand the small mosques named after Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Lady Fatimah (s.a.) and Salman, together known as the Seven Mosques.
tips: Pray two rak'at in the mosque and supplicate, as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) supplicated here for victory.
The Mosque of the Two Qiblahs (Masjid al-Qiblatayn), where the qiblah was changed from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, is a short drive to the west.

features.name: Tomb of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
features.note: In his house, now the chamber under the Green Dome.

ziyarat.note: After the ziyarat.

ziyarat.label: Farewell to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
ziyarat.note: Before leaving Madinah.

features.name: House of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.)
features.note: Her house adjoined the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) chamber on its north side and is now inside the same enclosure; it is one of the places where she is said to be buried.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.): With the Longer Form

features.name: The Rawdah
features.note: Between the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) tomb and his minbar, which he called one of the gardens of Paradise; one of the places where Lady Fatimah (s.a.) is said to be buried.

ziyarat.note: Most scholars recite it from the Rawdah.

features.name: Minbar of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
features.note: A later minbar standing where the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) own minbar stood, at the western end of the Rawdah.

features.name: Bab al-Salam
features.note: Gate 1, on the west side near the qiblah wall; pilgrims traditionally enter here and walk along the qiblah wall to the tomb.

features.name: Bab al-Rahma
features.note: Gate 3, one of the old gates on the west side.

features.name: Bab Jibril
features.note: Gate 40, on the east side beside the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) chamber.

features.name: Bab al-Baqi
features.note: Gate 41, on the east side near the qiblah wall, the gate nearest al-Baqi; the way past the tomb leaves the mosque here.

features.name: King Fahd Gate
features.note: Gates 20 to 22, the main entrance on the north side.

features.name: Graves of the Four Imams (a.s.)
features.note: Imam Hasan, Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) lie together inside this low octagonal wall, with Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib; their dome stood here until 1926.

ziyarat.note: After the ziyarat of the Imams (a.s.).

ziyarat.label: Farewell to the Four Imams (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: When leaving al-Baqi.

features.name: Gate of al-Baqi
features.note: The cemetery's main gate, in its western wall facing the Prophet's Mosque.

ziyarat.label: Greeting the Believers Buried Here
ziyarat.note: On entering the cemetery.

cities.name: Makkah al-Mukarramah
cities.about: The city of the Kaaba and the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) birthplace, where pilgrims come for Hajj and Umrah. Their rites are not part of this guide. Beyond Masjid al-Haram, Shia pilgrims visit Jannat al-Mu'alla, where Lady Khadijah (s.a.), Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) and Hazrat Abdul Muttalib (a.s.) are buried, and the site of the house where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was born.
tips: Hajj fills the city in the first half of Dhul Hijjah; outside Hajj, Ramazan, especially its last ten nights, is the busiest time for Umrah.
Jannat al-Mu'alla is a short walk or ride north of Masjid al-Haram, past the Masjid al-Jinn.
As in Madinah, local rules restrict acts at graves; pilgrims recite the ziyarat quietly from a distance.

sites.name: Masjid al-Haram
sites.about: The Sacred Mosque around the Kaaba, the qiblah of every prayer, built by Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) and Ismail (a.s.). Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was born inside the Kaaba. The rites of Hajj and Umrah performed here are outside this guide; follow a reliable manual of your marja for them.

buried.name: Prophet Ismail (a.s.) and Lady Hajar
buried.note: By narration buried in the Hijr Ismail, the semicircular enclosure beside the Kaaba.

tips: For the rites of Hajj and Umrah, and for praying in the Hijr Ismail, follow the manual of your marja.
Carry a small bag for your shoes; the racks at the gates fill up and the mosque's gates are far apart.

sites.name: Jannat al-Mu'alla
sites.about: The old cemetery of Makkah, also called al-Hajun, second in honour after al-Baqi, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) often visited. Here lie his first wife Lady Khadijah (s.a.), his uncle and guardian Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), his grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib (a.s.) and earlier forefathers. Their domes were demolished in 1925.

ziyarat.label: Greeting the Believers Buried Here
ziyarat.note: On entering the cemetery.

buried.name: Lady Khadijah al-Kubra (s.a.)
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) first wife, the first to believe in him and the mother of Lady Fatimah (s.a.); she died in the tenth year of the mission.

buried.name: Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.)
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) uncle and protector, father of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.); he died in the same year as Lady Khadijah (s.a.), the Year of Grief.

buried.name: Hazrat Abdul Muttalib (a.s.)
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) grandfather and guardian in his childhood, chief of Makkah.

buried.name: Abd Manaf
buried.note: Forefather of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.).

buried.name: Qasim, Son of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
buried.note: The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) son by Lady Khadijah (s.a.), who died as a child.

tips: The graves are behind walls and railings; pilgrims recite the ziyarats from outside, facing the graves.
Pilgrims also recite al-Fatihah for Lady Khadijah (s.a.) and the others buried here.

sites.name: Birthplace of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
sites.about: By the tradition most scholars accept, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was born on this spot in Suq al-Layl, east of Masjid al-Haram. The house was later made a mosque, and since about 1951 the site has been the Makkah al-Mukarramah Library.
tips: The building is a library and is not open for prayer; pilgrims send salawat outside it, especially on 17 Rabi al-Awwal, the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) birthday.

cities.name: Najaf al-Ashraf
cities.about: Najaf is the city of Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (a.s.), who was buried here in secret in 40 AH, and for a thousand years the home of the Shia seminary founded around his shrine by Shaykh al-Tusi. North of the shrine lies Wadi al-Salam, the vast cemetery where believers have long asked to be buried. Kufa, where Imam Ali (a.s.) lived and was struck, has grown into one city with Najaf, and its mosques are a short drive away.
tips: Most pilgrims stay in the old city around the shrine and walk to it; Wadi al-Salam starts just north of the shrine, beyond Bab al-Tusi.
The busiest days are the martyrdom of Imam Ali (a.s.) on 19-21 Ramadan, Eid al-Ghadir on 18 Dhul Hijjah and the Mab'ath on 27 Rajab, when special ziyarats of Imam Ali (a.s.) are recited.
In the first weeks of Safar many pilgrims set out on foot from Najaf to Karbala for Arbaeen (20 Safar), along the road lined with mawkibs that host walkers.
Plan the Kufa mosques (Masjid al-Kufa, Masjid al-Sahla) as a half day of their own; Masjid al-Sahla is best visited between Maghrib and Isha.
Shoes are left at a kishwaniyya by each gate and bags are searched at the entrances, so carry little; women are expected to wear a full abaya or chador inside the shrines.

sites.name: Shrine of Imam Ali (a.s.)
sites.about: The tomb of Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), martyred in Kufa on 21 Ramadan 40 AH and buried by his sons at night outside the city. Its place was kept hidden until the Imams revealed it, and Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) visited it with his companions. By narration Prophets Adam and Nuh (a.s.) lie with him, and the ziyarat greets them as his two companions. The building took its present form under the Safavids; around its courtyard lie many of the great scholars of the Shia.

ziyarat.note: The other forms reported for this shrine, one per tab.
The six-unit ziyarat prayer and the duas after it.
At the head side of Imam Ali (a.s.)'s tomb, facing Karbala.
On Eid al-Ghadir, 18 Dhul Hijjah.
Also on 18 Dhul Hijjah.

buried.name: Prophet Adam (a.s.)
buried.note: By narration buried beside Imam Ali (a.s.); the ziyarat greets him, and two units of the ziyarat prayer are offered for him.

buried.name: Prophet Nuh (a.s.)
buried.note: By narration buried beside Imam Ali (a.s.); greeted in the ziyarat with Adam (a.s.), with two units of the ziyarat prayer for him.

buried.name: Allamah al-Hilli
buried.note: Hasan ibn Yusuf, the great jurist and theologian of Hilla; buried in the room on the north side of the Golden Iwan, beside its northern minaret, on the right as you enter the haram.

buried.name: Al-Muqaddas al-Ardabili
buried.note: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ardabili, jurist famed for his piety; buried in the room on the south side of the Golden Iwan, opposite Allamah al-Hilli.

buried.name: Shaykh Murtada al-Ansari
buried.note: Author of al-Rasa'il and al-Makasib, still the core texts of the seminary; buried in the courtyard chamber beside Bab al-Qibla.

buried.name: Muhaddith al-Nuri
buried.note: Mirza Husayn al-Nuri, compiler of Mustadrak al-Wasa'il; buried in one of the chambers of the courtyard.

buried.name: Shaykh Abbas al-Qummi
buried.note: Compiler of Mafatih al-Jinan, the source of most of the ziyarats in this app; buried beside his teacher Muhaddith al-Nuri.

buried.name: Akhund al-Khurasani
buried.note: Muhammad Kazim al-Khurasani, author of Kifayat al-Usul; buried in one of the chambers of the shrine's courtyard.

buried.name: Sayyid Muhammad Kazim al-Yazdi
buried.note: Author of al-Urwa al-Wuthqa, the book of rulings on which most later jurists wrote their glosses; buried in the courtyard.

buried.name: Sayyid Abu al-Hasan al-Isfahani
buried.note: The leading marja of his time; buried in one of the chambers of the courtyard.

buried.name: Sayyid Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei
buried.note: The leading marja of his time; buried with his sons in the chamber beside Masjid al-Khadra, which opens off the shrine's courtyard.

buried.name: Adud al-Dawla
buried.note: The Buyid ruler who rebuilt the shrine and asked to be buried near Imam Ali (a.s.).

tips: Recite the permission to enter at the gate of the sanctuary; the First Ziyarat begins once you stand facing the tomb.
The ziyarat prayer here is six units: two for Imam Ali (a.s.) and four as a gift to Prophets Adam and Nuh (a.s.).

Masjid al-Ras, on the south side of the Abu Talib portico, marks where by narration the head of Imam Husayn (a.s.) was buried beside his father; the [ziyarat of the head](AK7) is recited at the head side of Imam Ali (a.s.)'s tomb, where Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) prayed and recited it.
The scholars' chambers line the courtyard walls; Shaykh al-Ansari's is beside Bab al-Qibla, and Allamah al-Hilli and al-Muqaddas al-Ardabili lie on either side of the Golden Iwan.

sites.name: Masjid and Tomb of Shaykh al-Tusi
sites.about: Just outside Bab al-Tusi, the north gate of the shrine's courtyard, stands the house of Shaykh al-Tusi, which he willed to become a mosque and where he was buried. He came to Najaf from Baghdad in 448 AH and founded its seminary; two of the four books of Shia hadith are his. Sayyid Mahdi Bahr al-Ulum, who identified many of the holy places of Najaf and Kufa, is buried here too.

buried.name: Shaykh al-Tusi
buried.note: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, Shaykh al-Ta'ifa, author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam and al-Istibsar; buried in his own house, now the mosque.

buried.name: Sayyid Mahdi Bahr al-Ulum
buried.note: Jurist renowned for his piety, who preserved the graves in the shrine's courtyard from removal; buried beside Shaykh al-Tusi.

tips: Leave the courtyard by Bab al-Tusi; the mosque is immediately beside the gate, on the way to Wadi al-Salam.

sites.name: Wadi al-Salam Cemetery
sites.about: Wadi al-Salam, the Valley of Peace, stretches north and west of the shrine and is among the largest cemeteries in the world. By narration Imam Ali (a.s.) said that the souls of the believers gather here, and Shia families have brought their dead to be buried near him for centuries. It holds the tomb attributed to Prophets Hud and Salih (a.s.) and the maqams of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) in its northern part.

buried.name: Sayyid Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr
buried.note: Jurist and philosopher, author of Falsafatuna and Iqtisaduna, executed in Baghdad and buried in Wadi al-Salam, where a shrine now marks his grave.

tips: The cemetery is a maze of graves and lanes; enter from the old city near the shrine and keep to the main paths or go with someone who knows it.
Greet the believers buried here and recite al-Fatihah and Surah al-Qadr for them, as in [Visiting the Graves of the Faithful Believers](G29).
Avoid the open cemetery in the midday heat of summer and carry water.

sites.name: Tomb of Prophets Hud and Salih (a.s.)
sites.about: A domed shrine at the edge of Wadi al-Salam, a short walk north of Imam Ali (a.s.)'s shrine, holding two graves attributed by narration to Prophet Hud (a.s.), sent to the people of 'Ad, and Prophet Salih (a.s.), sent to Thamud. The building was first raised in the time of Sayyid Mahdi Bahr al-Ulum and has been renewed since.

buried.name: Prophet Hud (a.s.)
buried.note: Sent to the people of 'Ad; by narration buried here in Wadi al-Salam.

buried.name: Prophet Salih (a.s.)
buried.note: Sent to the people of Thamud; by narration buried beside Hud (a.s.).

tips: It is the nearest part of Wadi al-Salam to the old city, so many pilgrims visit it on the way into the cemetery.

sites.name: Masjid al-Hannanah
sites.about: A mosque on the old road between Najaf and Kufa, also called Masjid al-Ras. By narration the column here bowed as Imam Ali (a.s.)'s body was carried past to his grave, and the head of Imam Husayn (a.s.) was set down here on its way to Ibn Ziyad in Kufa. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) is reported to have stopped and prayed here, and pilgrims pray and recite the ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.).
tips: It is a few hundred metres from the tomb of Kumayl ibn Ziyad, and the two are usually visited together on the way to Kufa.

sites.name: Tomb of Kumayl ibn Ziyad
sites.about: Kumayl ibn Ziyad al-Nakha'i was a close companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), who taught him the supplication now called [Dua Kumayl](E31). He was killed on the order of al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf and buried at al-Thawiyya, between Najaf and Kufa, next to Masjid al-Hannanah. Pilgrims recite al-Fatihah for him here, and many recite his dua.

buried.name: Kumayl ibn Ziyad al-Nakha'i
buried.note: Companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), martyred by al-Hajjaj.

tips: If you have time, recite [Dua Kumayl](E31) here, the supplication he learned from Imam Ali (a.s.).

features.name: Zarih of Imam Ali (a.s.)
features.note: By narration Prophets Adam (a.s.) and Nuh (a.s.) are buried with him here.

ziyarat.note: The other forms reported for this shrine, one per tab.
The six-unit ziyarat prayer and the duas after it.
At the head side of the tomb, facing Karbala.
On Eid al-Ghadir, 18 Dhul Hijjah.

features.name: Tomb of Allamah al-Hilli
features.note: In the room on the north side of the Golden Iwan, beside its northern minaret.

features.name: Tomb of Muqaddas Ardabili
features.note: In the room on the south side of the Golden Iwan, opposite Allamah al-Hilli.

features.name: The Golden Iwan
features.note: The gilded porch on the east side of the haram, between its two gold minarets, facing Bab al-Sa'a. The Golden Door in its middle leads into the haram.

features.name: Bab al-Sa'a (Bab al-Rida)
features.note: Also called Bab al-Imam al-Reza (a.s.), a name it took when it reopened, restored and gilded, in 2023. The Clock Gate, the largest gate of the courtyard, in the middle of its east side, under the clock tower.

features.name: Bab Muslim ibn Aqil
features.note: A smaller gate on the east side, just north of Bab al-Sa'a. Opened in 1252 AH; once called Bab al-Abayjiyya.

features.name: Bab al-Tusi
features.note: The north gate, on the way to the tomb of Shaykh al-Tusi. Beside it is the great northern iwan (the Yazdi Iwan), which was the gate in the Safavid plan.

features.name: Bab al-Qibla
features.note: The south gate, the smallest of the main gates. Beside it is the great southern iwan (the Hububi Iwan), the original qibla gate.

features.name: Bab al-Faraj
features.note: The west gate, opened in Ottoman times; also called al-Bab al-Sultani and Bab al-Amara. It faces Sahn Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.).

features.name: Sahn Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.)
features.note: The large new courtyard on the west side of the shrine, with prayer halls on levels below ground. Bab al-Faraj opens onto it.

features.name: Masjid and Tomb of Shaykh al-Tusi

cities.name: Kufa
cities.about: Kufa was the capital of Imam Ali (a.s.) during his caliphate and the city where he was struck in the mihrab of its mosque on 19 Ramadan 40 AH. Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.) was martyred here as Imam Husayn (a.s.)'s envoy. The Imams counted Masjid al-Kufa among the four great mosques of Islam and praised Masjid al-Sahla as a place where prayers are answered. Today it is joined to Najaf, about 10 km east of the shrine.
tips: Most pilgrims come for the day from Najaf; start at Masjid al-Kufa, which holds the tombs of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.) and Hani ibn Urwah (a.s.), then visit the House of Imam Ali (a.s.) and Maytham al-Tammar next to it.
The acts of Masjid al-Kufa are a long sequence of prayers at its stations; allow a few hours and bring the app's entries open on your phone.
Go to Masjid al-Sahla in the evening: the acts there are best between Maghrib and Isha, especially on the night before Wednesday (Tuesday night), when it is very full.
Masjid al-Kufa is crowded on 19-21 Ramadan, the nights Imam Ali (a.s.) was struck and passed away, and on Thursday nights for Dua Kumayl.

sites.name: Masjid al-Kufa
sites.about: One of the four great mosques of Islam: by narration prophets from Adam to Ibrahim (a.s.) prayed here and Nuh (a.s.) built the Ark on its ground. Imam Ali (a.s.) taught, judged and led prayers here, and was struck by Ibn Muljam in its mihrab during the dawn prayer of 19 Ramadan 40 AH. Its stations (maqams) of the prophets and Imams, its seat of judgement (Dikkat al-Qada) and the place of the washtub (Bayt al-Tasht) each have their own prayers.

ziyarat.note: Entering the mosque, then the stations in order, ending at the mihrab.
Done last of all, after the station of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.).

ziyarat.label: Munajat of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) in Masjid al-Kufa
ziyarat.note: The whispered prayer recited in this mosque.

tips: The mihrab where Imam Ali (a.s.) was struck is at the front of the prayer hall, on the qibla side; its prayer is the last tab of the mosque's acts.
The station of Prophet Adam (a.s.) is at the seventh column and the station of Gabriel at the fifth, as the mosque's acts describe.
The station of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) is near the shrine of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.).

sites.name: Shrine of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.)
sites.about: Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.), cousin of Imam Husayn (a.s.), came to Kufa as his envoy, was betrayed and was killed by Ibn Ziyad on 9 Dhul Hijjah 60 AH, the Day of Arafah, before the Imam reached Iraq. He is buried under the golden dome on the eastern side of Masjid al-Kufa, next to the old governor's palace where he was killed. Al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi, who later rose to avenge Karbala, is buried in the same complex.

buried.name: Al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
buried.note: Led the uprising in Kufa that punished the killers of Imam Husayn (a.s.); killed in 67 AH and buried at the back of the shrine of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.).

tips: Enter the shrine from inside Masjid al-Kufa, by its eastern side; Mukhtar's grave is reached through the same complex.

sites.name: Tomb of Hani ibn Urwah (a.s.)
sites.about: Hani ibn Urwah (a.s.), an elder of the tribe of Murad, sheltered Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.) in his house in Kufa and was killed by Ibn Ziyad for refusing to give him up, in 60 AH. His domed tomb stands against the eastern wall of Masjid al-Kufa, a few steps north of Muslim's shrine.
tips: Visit him straight after Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.); the two shrines are next to each other.

sites.name: House of Imam Ali (a.s.)
sites.about: The modest house beside Masjid al-Kufa where Imam Ali (a.s.) lived with his family during his caliphate. By tradition he was carried here after being struck in the mosque and passed away here on 21 Ramadan 40 AH.
tips: It is just south of Masjid al-Kufa, a short walk from the tomb of Maytham al-Tammar.

sites.name: Tomb of Maytham al-Tammar
sites.about: Maytham al-Tammar, the date-seller of Kufa, was a close companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), who foretold to him how he would die. He was crucified on the order of Ibn Ziyad shortly before Karbala in 60 AH, proclaiming the virtues of Imam Ali (a.s.) to the end. His shrine stands a little west of Masjid al-Kufa.

buried.name: Maytham al-Tammar
buried.note: Companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), martyred by Ibn Ziyad in Kufa.

sites.name: Masjid al-Sahla
sites.about: A great mosque on the north-west of Kufa that, by narration, was the house of Prophet Idris (a.s.) and of Ibrahim (a.s.), and will be the home of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) after his reappearance. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) said that whoever prays two units here between Maghrib and Isha with a need will have it met. Stations (maqams) inside mark Ibrahim, Idris, Khidr (a.s.), Imam al-Sadiq, Imam Zayn al-Abidin and Imam al-Mahdi.
tips: Come between Maghrib and Isha, ideally on the night before Wednesday (Tuesday night), as Sayyid Ibn Tawus advised.

The station of Ibrahim (a.s.) is in the north-west corner, Idris (a.s.) in the south-west, Khidr (a.s.) in the south-east corner and the Maqam of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) in the middle of the southern side.

sites.name: Masjids of Zayd and Sa'sa'ah ibn Sawhan
sites.about: Two small old mosques beside Masjid al-Sahla, named after the brothers Zayd and Sa'sa'ah ibn Sawhan, companions of Imam Ali (a.s.). Zayd was martyred fighting for him at the Battle of the Camel, and the dua prayed at his mosque is the one he used to recite in his night prayers. Scholars report that Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) was seen praying two units in Masjid Sa'sa'ah in Rajab and reciting the dua that begins "Allahumma ya dha al-minan".

ziyarat.label: Dua Ya Dhal Minan (Masjid Sa'sa'ah)
ziyarat.note: Especially in Rajab, after two units of prayer.

tips: Visit both straight after Masjid al-Sahla; Masjid Zayd lies on its south-west side and Masjid Sa'sa'ah close by.

features.name: Maqam of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)
features.note: The centre of the mosque, also called Dikkat al-Mi'raj, where by tradition the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed on the night of the Ascension.

features.name: Mihrab of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)
features.note: Where Imam Ali (a.s.) was struck by Ibn Muljam's sword at the dawn prayer.

features.name: Maqams of Ibrahim (a.s.) and Khizr (a.s.)
features.note: The mosque places it at the seventh column on the side of the Kinda gates, as narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.); the acts from Mafatih al-Jinan call it the fourth column.

features.name: Maqam of Prophet Nuh (a.s.)
features.note: Beside the minbar of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). The mosque gives here the same prayers that the linked acts give for the Seat of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.).

features.name: Dikkat al-Qadha
features.note: The Seat of Judgement, where Imam Ali (a.s.) sat to judge. Its acts are done last of all.

features.name: Bayt al-Tasht
features.note: The Place of the Wash-Tub, beside the Seat of Judgement.

features.name: Tomb of al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
features.note: At the back of the shrine of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.).

features.name: Bab al-Thu'ban
features.note: Also called Bab al-Fil; the one old gate of the mosque still standing.

features.name: Centre of the Mosque
features.note: By tradition the maqams of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) and Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) are here, in the middle of the mosque.

cities.name: Karbala
cities.about: Karbala is where Imam Husayn (a.s.), his family and companions were martyred on Ashura, 10 Muharram 61 AH, and where they are buried. Its two golden shrines, of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and of his brother Hazrat Abbas (a.s.), face each other across the open walkway of Bayn al-Haramayn. The Imams urged their followers never to abandon this ziyarat, and it is made on foot from all over Iraq for Arbaeen.
tips: Most pilgrims stay within walking distance of Bayn al-Haramayn and move between the two shrines on foot.

The largest gatherings are on Ashura (10 Muharram) and Arbaeen (20 Safar), when millions arrive and the area around the shrines is packed for days; 15 Sha'ban, the Day of Arafah (9 Dhul Hijjah) and Thursday nights are also very full.
The ziyarats of Imam Husayn (a.s.) are recited without perfume, in a state of grief, after ghusl; the etiquettes are in [Etiquettes of the Journey to Imam Husayn (a.s.)](AG2).
The Mukhayyam (camp) and Tall al-Zaynabiyya are a few minutes' walk west of Imam Husayn (a.s.)'s shrine; the shrine of al-Hurr al-Riyahi is a short drive west of the city.

sites.name: Shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.)
sites.about: The tomb of Imam Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), grandson of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), martyred here on Ashura, 10 Muharram 61 AH. By tradition he was buried by his son Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) with the help of the Banu Asad, with his son Ali al-Akbar at his feet and the martyrs of his family and companions beyond. The ground around the tomb, al-Ha'ir, has its own rulings and merits, and the narrations on the reward of this ziyarat are countless.

ziyarat.note: Before setting out, at the Euphrates and on entering the shrine.
The full method from Mafatih al-Jinan: ghusl, permission to enter, the ziyarat, its prayer, then Ali al-Akbar (a.s.) and the martyrs.
Six more forms, one per tab, for any day.
At the feet of Imam Husayn (a.s.), where Ali al-Akbar (a.s.) is buried.
Facing the martyrs' grave, beyond Ali al-Akbar (a.s.).
At his tomb inside the shrine.
The ziyarat prayer at the head side, the tasbihs and the duas after the ziyarat.
Especially on Ashura, 10 Muharram, and on any day.
Another ziyarat for Ashura.
On Arbaeen, 20 Safar, in the forenoon.
On 1 and 15 Rajab and 15 Sha'ban.
On the night of 15 Rajab.
On 15 Sha'ban.
On the Qadr nights of Ramazan, and on the days of the two Eids.
On the nights before Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
On the Day of Arafah, 9 Dhul Hijjah.

buried.name: Hazrat Ali al-Akbar (a.s.)
buried.note: Eldest son of Imam Husayn (a.s.), the first of the Banu Hashim to be martyred on Ashura; buried at his father's feet.

buried.name: Hazrat Ali al-Asghar (a.s.)
buried.note: The infant son of Imam Husayn (a.s.), killed by an arrow in his father's arms; buried with his father.

buried.name: The Martyrs of Karbala (a.s.)
buried.note: The men of the Banu Hashim and the companions killed on Ashura, buried together in one grave beyond the feet of Imam Husayn (a.s.).

buried.name: Habib ibn Mazahir (a.s.)
buried.note: Elderly companion of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.) who came from Kufa to fight for Imam Husayn (a.s.); buried apart from the others, to the right of the main qibla entrance of the sanctuary.

buried.name: Sayyid Ibrahim al-Mujab
buried.note: Grandson of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) and the first custodian of the shrine; called al-Mujab, "the answered", because by tradition his greeting at the tomb was answered. Buried in the portico named after him.

buried.name: Al-Wahid al-Bihbahani
buried.note: Muhammad Baqir al-Bihbahani, who renewed the study of usul al-fiqh in Karbala; buried in the eastern part of the shrine.

buried.name: Sayyid Ali al-Tabataba'i (Sahib al-Riyad)
buried.note: Author of Riyad al-Masa'il and student of al-Wahid al-Bihbahani; buried beside his teacher.

tips: Ali al-Akbar (a.s.) is at the feet of Imam Husayn (a.s.), inside the same enclosure; the martyrs' grave is just beyond him.
Pray the ziyarat prayer at the head side, stepping back a little so as not to stand level with the tomb; praying behind the tomb is also valid.
At the head side recite the tasbih of Imam Ali (a.s.), and at the feet the tasbih of Lady Fatimah (s.a.), as in the post-ziyarat acts.
Habib ibn Mazahir (a.s.)'s grave is in the portico by the qibla entrance of the sanctuary, about ten metres from the tomb of Imam Husayn (a.s.).

sites.name: Shrine of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.)
sites.about: The tomb of Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas ibn Ali (a.s.), son of Imam Ali (a.s.) and Umm al-Baneen, standard-bearer of Imam Husayn (a.s.). He was martyred on Ashura by the river while bringing water for the thirsty children, after both his hands were cut off, and was buried where he fell, apart from the other martyrs. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) taught the ziyarat to be recited at the gate of his shrine.

ziyarat.note: From Mafatih al-Jinan, with its prayer, dua and farewell.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) (as commonly recited)

tips: The ziyarat of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) is recited standing at the gate of the shrine, then you enter and stand at the tomb.
Two small shrines mark where his hands fell: Kaff al-Abbas al-Yamin (right hand) north-east of the shrine and Kaff al-Abbas al-Yasar (left hand) south-east of it, both a few minutes' walk away.
Pray two units of the ziyarat prayer at the head side, then supplicate; the farewell is the last part of the ziyarat entry.

sites.name: Bayn al-Haramayn
sites.about: The open, covered walkway of a few hundred metres between the shrines of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and Hazrat Abbas (a.s.), where pilgrims pass constantly between the two. On Ashura and Arbaeen the processions of mourners (mawkibs) pass through it, and the Tuwairij run of the afternoon of Ashura comes through it to Imam Husayn (a.s.)'s shrine.
tips: From the middle of Bayn al-Haramayn both domes are in sight; many pilgrims greet both Imam Husayn (a.s.) and Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) from here when the shrines are too full to enter.

sites.name: Tall al-Zaynabiyya
sites.about: A small domed shrine just west of Imam Husayn (a.s.)'s shrine on the rise where, by tradition, Lady Zainab (s.a.) stood on Ashura watching the battle and calling out to her brother as the tents were set on fire.

sites.name: Al-Mukhayyam (The Camp of Imam Husayn (a.s.))
sites.about: A building south-west of Imam Husayn (a.s.)'s shrine marking where the tents of the Imam, his family and companions stood, which were set on fire on the afternoon of Ashura. The camp itself spread over a wider area, so the building is a marker of it rather than its exact bounds.

sites.name: Shrine of al-Hurr al-Riyahi (a.s.)
sites.about: Al-Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi (a.s.) led the troops sent to stop Imam Husayn (a.s.) on his way to Kufa, then on the morning of Ashura turned to the Imam, repented and was martyred defending him. The Imam said he was free (hurr), as his mother had named him, in this world and the next. His shrine stands a few kilometres west of the old city; some scholars doubt the site, holding that he lies with the other martyrs.

buried.name: Al-Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi (a.s.)
buried.note: Martyred on Ashura after joining Imam Husayn (a.s.).

tips: Take a taxi from the old city; the shrine is in the al-Hurr district, west of Karbala.

ziyarat.note: The ziyarat prayer at the head side, and the duas after it.

features.name: Tomb of Hazrat Ali al-Akbar (a.s.)
features.note: At the feet of Imam Husayn (a.s.).

features.name: Tomb of the Martyrs of Karbala (a.s.)
features.note: The companions and family of Imam Husayn (a.s.) martyred with him lie together here.

features.name: Maqam al-Madhbah
features.note: Marks the place where, by tradition, Imam Husayn (a.s.) was martyred.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) (as commonly recited)

features.name: Maqam of the Right Hand of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.)
features.note: Marks the place where, by tradition, the right hand of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) fell.

features.name: Maqam of the Left Hand of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.)
features.note: Marks the place where, by tradition, the left hand of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) fell.

features.name: Clock Tower
features.note: Above the qibla gate of the shrine of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.); a landmark pilgrims often meet at.

cities.name: Musayyib
cities.about: A town on the Euphrates about 35 km north-east of Karbala, between Karbala and Baghdad. Pilgrims stop here for the shrine attributed to the two young sons of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.).
tips: Musayyib is usually visited as a short stop on the road between Karbala and Baghdad or Kazimayn; the shrine lies a few kilometres east of the town centre.

sites.name: Shrine of the Sons of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.)
sites.about: A twin-domed shrine attributed to Muhammad and Ibrahim, the two young sons of Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.). By the narration in Shaykh al-Saduq's al-Amali, they were captured after Karbala, escaped from prison in Kufa and were killed on the bank of the Euphrates. Some sources hold that the two boys were not Muslim's own sons, and their ages differ between accounts.

buried.name: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.)
buried.note: The elder of the two brothers, by tradition killed with his brother on the Euphrates.

buried.name: Ibrahim ibn Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.)
buried.note: The younger brother, buried beside him.

cities.name: Kazimayn, Baghdad
cities.about: Kazimayn (al-Kazimiyya) is the shrine town on the west bank of the Tigris in northern Baghdad, grown up around the graves of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) and his grandson Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (a.s.). The site began as the Quraysh cemetery laid out beside the Abbasid round city, and the two Imams lie under one double-domed shrine. Several of the great early Shia scholars are buried with them.
tips: Most pilgrims stay in the old quarter around the shrine and walk to it; the lanes and markets leading to the gates are busy until late at night.

The heaviest crowds come on 25 Rajab, the anniversary of Imam al-Kazim (a.s.)'s martyrdom, when many walk from all over Baghdad; the end of Dhul Qa'dah (Imam al-Jawad (a.s.)'s martyrdom) is also busy.
Baghdad's other ziyarat sites - the tombs of the Four Deputies and of Shaykh al-Kulayni across the river, and Masjid Buratha on the way - are easily combined with a stay here.
Samarra, with Balad on the way, and Salman Pak (Mada'in) are usually visited as day trips from Kazimayn.
Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) is known as Bab al-Hawa'ij (the door of needs): pilgrims traditionally bring their requests to him.

sites.name: Shrine of Imam Musa al-Kazim and Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (a.s.)
sites.about: The shrine of the seventh Imam, Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), who died in the prison of Harun al-Rashid in Baghdad in 183 AH, and of the ninth Imam, Muhammad al-Jawad (a.s.), buried beside his grandfather in 220 AH. The two graves lie side by side under one shrine with twin golden domes; the present building goes back largely to the Safavid rebuilding of the 16th century. Begin with [Izn-e-Dukhool](B6), visit each Imam with his own ziyarat, and end with the farewell common to both in [the shared ziyarat](AH9).

ziyarat.note: At the gate of the shrine.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) (by Shaykh al-Mufid)
Second Ziyarat of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.)
Ziyarat of Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: Opens with the entry rites recited at the shrine's gate.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Imam al-Jawad (a.s.) from Baqiyat al-Salihat
Dua after the Ziyarat of Imam al-Jawad (a.s.)

ziyarat.note: Can be recited at the shrine of any of the Imams (a.s.).
Addresses both Imams together and ends with the farewell (wida).

buried.name: Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.)
buried.note: The seventh Imam, martyred in the prison of Harun al-Rashid; buried in the Quraysh cemetery, around which the shrine grew.

buried.name: Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (a.s.)
buried.note: The ninth Imam, grandson of Imam al-Kazim (a.s.), buried beside him under the same shrine.

buried.name: Shaykh al-Mufid
buried.note: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, the leading Shia theologian and jurist of Baghdad; his body was moved here from his house and laid near the feet of the two Imams, beside his teacher Ibn Qulawayh.

buried.name: Ibn Qulawayh al-Qummi
buried.note: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, author of Kamil al-Ziyarat and teacher of Shaykh al-Mufid; buried beside him in the shrine (one later scholar placed his grave in Qom).

buried.name: Khwaja Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
buried.note: Theologian, philosopher and astronomer, author of Tajrid al-I'tiqad; died in Baghdad and was buried in the shrine at his own request.

tips: Stand facing the tomb with your back to the qiblah for the ziyarat, then pray the two rak'ats of ziyarat for each Imam; [Surah Ya-Sin](A40) and [Surah Ar-Rahman](A59) after al-Fatihah are recommended.
The two Imams lie side by side in one shrine: greet each with his own ziyarat, and recite the shared one (with its farewell) at the end.
Men's and women's entrances and the shoe-keeping (kishwaniyya) are at the gates of the courtyard; follow the signs and the shrine staff.
Shaykh al-Mufid's grave is near the feet of the two Imams; ask the shrine staff to point out his and Khwaja Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's graves and recite al-Fatihah for them.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/ (العتبة الكاظمية, مرقد الامام موسى الكاظم)

sites.name: Tombs of Sayyid al-Murtada and Sayyid al-Radi
sites.about: Two small shrines in the old quarter just south-east of the Kazimayn shrine, reached from its Bab al-Qibla side, are visited as the graves of the brothers al-Sharif al-Murtada and al-Sharif al-Radi. Where the brothers are buried is disputed: they were first buried in their house in Baghdad, and some reports say they were later carried to Karbala and buried near Imam Husayn (a.s.). The al-Murtada shrine was taken down in 2022 and rebuilt.

ziyarat.label: At the Grave of a Believer
ziyarat.note: The general visit to a believer's grave.

buried.name: Sayyid al-Murtada
buried.note: Alam al-Huda, the leading Shia theologian and jurist of Baghdad after Shaykh al-Mufid; one of the places where he is said to be buried.

buried.name: Sayyid al-Radi
buried.note: Compiler of Nahj al-Balagha and elder brother of al-Murtada; his shrine stands beside his brother's, one of the places where he is said to be buried.

tips: Both tombs are a few minutes' walk from the shrine's Bab al-Qibla, on the street named after al-Sharif al-Radi.
Recite al-Fatihah for them; there is no special ziyarat for these graves.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/ (مرقد الشريف المرتضى, مرقد الشريف الرضي)

features.name: Zarih of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.)
features.note: One zarih holds both Imams: Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) lies at its southern end, under the southern dome.

ziyarat.label: Ziyarat of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) (by Shaykh al-Mufid)
Second Ziyarat of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.)

cities.name: Baghdad
cities.about: Baghdad, the Abbasid capital founded by al-Mansur, was where the Four Deputies (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'a) of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) lived and carried his letters to the Shia during the Minor Occultation (260-329 AH), and where they are buried. The city also holds the tomb of Shaykh al-Kulayni, compiler of al-Kafi, and Masjid Buratha, where Imam Ali (a.s.) prayed. Kazimayn, on the city's north-western edge, is listed on its own.
tips: The deputies' tombs and Shaykh al-Kulayni's are on the east bank (Rusafa), in and around the old markets between al-Rashid Street and Shorja; some of the graves sit inside the lanes of the bazaar, so ask locally or go with a guide.
Masjid Buratha is on the west bank, on the way between Kazimayn and central Baghdad, and is easily visited from Kazimayn.
Mafatih al-Jinan gives one ziyarat for the deputies, reported from Husayn ibn Ruh, that is recited at the tomb of each of them, naming him.
Most pilgrims stay in Kazimayn and visit these sites in a single day across the river.

sites.name: Tomb of Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri (Khilani Mosque)
sites.arabicName: مرقد محمد بن عثمان العمري (جامع الخلاني)
sites.about: The Khilani Mosque on al-Jumhuriya Street, in the square named after it, holds the grave visited by Shia as that of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri, the second of the Four Deputies, who succeeded his father Uthman ibn Sa'id and died in 304 or 305 AH. Some historians attribute the grave to a Hanbali scholar instead. The mosque is cared for by Shia and is a centre of prayer in the heart of Rusafa.

ziyarat.note: Recited at the tomb of each deputy, naming him.

ziyarat.label: At the Grave of a Believer
ziyarat.note: The general visit to a believer's grave.

buried.name: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri
buried.note: Second deputy of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), son and successor of the first deputy; the grave in the mosque is visited as his.

tips: In the deputies' ziyarat, greet him by name: Muhammad ibn Uthman.
The mosque holds congregational prayers; visit the grave outside prayer times.

sites.name: Tomb of Shaykh al-Kulayni
sites.about: A small shrine in the al-Asifiyya mosque on the east bank of the Tigris, beside the old Mustansiriyya school and the Shuhada (old) bridge, is visited as the grave of Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni. He compiled al-Kafi, the foremost of the four books of Shia hadith, and died in Baghdad in 329 AH, the year the Major Occultation began. Some writers attribute the tomb to the Sufi al-Harith al-Muhasibi instead.

ziyarat.label: At the Grave of a Believer
ziyarat.note: The general visit to a believer's grave.

buried.name: Shaykh al-Kulayni
buried.note: Thiqat al-Islam, compiler of al-Kafi; the shrine in the al-Asifiyya mosque is visited as his grave.

tips: The tomb of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, the fourth deputy, is said to be near Shaykh al-Kulayni's; ask at the shrine for the way.
The shrine overlooks the river at the Rusafa end of the Shuhada bridge, next to the Mustansiriyya school.

sites.name: Masjid Buratha
sites.about: An ancient mosque on the west bank of Baghdad, on the road between Kazimayn and the city, built where a monastery once stood. By narration, Imam Ali (a.s.) stopped and prayed here on his return from the battle of Nahrawan, and a spring of cold, sweet water came up where he struck the ground. Mafatih al-Jinan recommends praying in it; the present building is modern (1954).
tips: Pray two rak'ats of greeting the mosque (tahiyyat al-masjid); a stone inside marks the place associated with Imam Ali (a.s.)'s prayer.
It is a short drive from Kazimayn and is often visited on the way into central Baghdad.

cities.name: Samarra
cities.about: Samarra (Surra-man-Ra'a), on the Tigris north of Baghdad, was built by the Abbasid caliph al-Mu'tasim as his capital. Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) was brought here and kept under watch, as was his son Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) after him; both are buried in their house, which is now the al-Askari Shrine. Beside it is the Sardab, the cellar linked with Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and the start of his occultation.
tips: Most pilgrims visit Samarra on a day trip from Kazimayn or Baghdad, often in organised groups, stopping at Balad for Sayyid Muhammad on the way.
The busiest days are 8 Rabi al-Awwal (martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (a.s.)), 3 Rajab (martyrdom of Imam al-Naqi (a.s.)) and 15 Shaban (birth of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)).
Visit the two Imams first, then go down to the Sardab; the same permission to enter ([Izn-e-Dukhool](B6)) serves both.
Most of the town's people are not Shia; keep to the shrine area and follow the guidance of your group and the shrine staff.

sites.name: Al-Askari Shrine (Imam Ali al-Naqi and Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.))
sites.about: The house of the tenth and eleventh Imams, Ali al-Naqi al-Hadi (a.s.) and al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), where both were buried; Lady Narjis, mother of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and Lady Hakimah, daughter of Imam al-Jawad (a.s.), lie in the same shrine. Its golden dome was destroyed in bombings in 2006 and 2007 and has since been rebuilt. Begin with [the ziyarat of both Imams together](AL1), then visit each Imam with his own ziyarat.

ziyarat.note: At the gate of the shrine.
Both Imams together; recited on arriving at the shrine and described in it as the most authentic form.

ziyarat.label: Permission to Enter and Ziyarat of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.)
Dua after the Ziyarat of Imam al-Askari (a.s.)

ziyarat.note: Can be recited at the shrine of any of the Imams (a.s.).
Prayer, dua and farewell (wida) to the two Imams at the end of the visit.

buried.name: Imam Ali al-Naqi al-Hadi (a.s.)
buried.note: The tenth Imam, brought to Samarra by the caliph al-Mutawakkil and kept there until his martyrdom; buried in his house.

buried.name: Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)
buried.note: The eleventh Imam, father of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.); buried beside his father.

buried.name: Lady Narjis (s.a.)
buried.note: Mother of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), buried in the shrine beside the two Imams.

buried.name: Lady Hakimah (s.a.)
buried.note: Daughter of Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (a.s.) and aunt of Imam al-Askari (a.s.), who was present at the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.); buried in the same shrine.

buried.name: Husayn ibn Ali al-Hadi
buried.note: Son of Imam al-Naqi (a.s.) and brother of Imam al-Askari (a.s.), buried in the shrine.

tips: Pray the ziyarat prayer at the tombs if you can reach them, or else in the mosque beside the Imams' house where they used to pray, as the [combined ziyarat](AL1) instructs.
Remember Lady Narjis (s.a.) and Lady Hakimah (s.a.) inside the same zarih; the corpus does not yet hold their own ziyarats, so a salam and al-Fatihah will do.
The Sardab is reached through the mosque that adjoins the shrine, under its own dome.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/ (مرقد الامامين علي الهادي والحسن العسكري)

sites.name: The Holy Sardab (Cellar of the Occultation)
sites.about: A cellar in the house of the two Imams, now under the mosque and blue dome beside the al-Askari Shrine, associated with Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.): by tradition the place where he worshipped and from which his occultation began. It is not a grave but a place of ziyarat and prayer for the living Imam, visited after the two Imams. The scholars of ziyarat give several forms to recite here, followed by a twelve-rak'at prayer gifted to the Imam.

ziyarat.note: Permission to enter the Sardab.

After the Fajr prayer.

tips: Go down placing the right foot first, as the ziyarats instruct; on 15 Shaban expect long queues to enter.
After the ziyarat, pray twelve rak'ats in pairs and gift them to Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), reciting the [Tasbih of Lady Fatimah (s.a.)](I9) after each pair.
Pray here for the Imam's reappearance before your own needs; [Dua Ahad](E18) and [Ziyarat Aal-e-Yasin](G1) are short enough to recite in the crowd.

features.note: The two Imams lie side by side under the golden dome; Lady Narjis (s.a.) and Lady Hakimah (s.a.) are buried with them under the same dome.

cities.name: Balad
cities.about: Balad is a town on the road from Baghdad to Samarra, about 85 km north of Baghdad. It is known for the shrine of Sayyid Muhammad, the eldest son of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.), who died in 252 AH and is buried here. Pilgrims usually stop here on the way to or from Samarra.
tips: Plan Balad as a stop on the Samarra day trip, on the way there or back.
Locals call Sayyid Muhammad Sab' al-Dujayl (the lion of Dujayl) and hold oaths sworn by him in great respect; keep to the shrine's customs.

sites.name: Shrine of Sayyid Muhammad, Son of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.)
sites.arabicName: مرقد السيد محمد بن الإمام علي الهادي
sites.about: The shrine of Abu Ja'far Muhammad, the eldest son of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) and brother of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). He was so honoured for his piety that many expected him to succeed his father, but he died in 252 AH, in his father's lifetime, and was buried here. Shia scholars hold him in high regard, and his shrine has long been a place of pilgrimage and of seeking needs.

buried.name: Sayyid Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hadi
buried.note: Eldest son of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.), known as Sab' al-Dujayl; buried at Balad, between Samarra and Baghdad.

tips: After his ziyarat, pray two rak'ats and gift them to him; many pilgrims also bring him their needs, as the people of the region have long done.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/ (مرقد السيد محمد بن الامام الهادي سبع الدجيل)

cities.name: Mada'in (Salman Pak)
cities.about: Mada'in, the old Sasanian capital Ctesiphon on the Tigris about 30 km south-east of Baghdad, was governed for the second caliph by Salman al-Farsi, who died and was buried here; the town around his shrine is called Salman Pak after him. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, also governor of Mada'in, and other companions lie in the same complex, and the ruined arch of the Sasanian palace (Taq Kasra) stands nearby.
tips: Mada'in is a half-day trip from Kazimayn or Baghdad; the shrine complex and Taq Kasra are a short walk apart.
Recite [Surah Al-Qadr](A101) seven times at Salman's tomb, as his ziyarat instructs, then pray and gift it to him.
The tombs of Hudhayfah and the others are in separate buildings of the same complex; visit them after Salman.

sites.name: Shrine of Salman al-Farsi
sites.about: The tomb of Salman al-Farsi, the Persian companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) of whom he said "Salman is one of us, the Ahl al-Bayt", and a loyal follower of Imam Ali (a.s.). By narration, Imam Ali (a.s.) came from Madinah to wash and bury him. In 1931 the remains of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and of two graves attributed to Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari and Tahir son of Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) were moved here from the Tigris bank, where water threatened them.

ziyarat.note: The ziyarat of Salman, from Misbah al-Za'ir and Tahdhib al-Ahkam, ending with his farewell.

buried.name: Salman al-Farsi (r.a.)
buried.note: Companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and of Imam Ali (a.s.), governor of Mada'in, where he died; buried in the main shrine.

buried.name: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman
buried.note: Companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), keeper of his confidences and governor of Mada'in, who urged its people to pledge allegiance to Imam Ali (a.s.); reburied in a tomb beside Salman's in 1931.

buried.name: Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari
buried.note: Companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the first pilgrim to Imam Husayn (a.s.)'s grave on the Arbaeen; a grave here bears his name, though most sources say he died and was buried in Madinah.

buried.name: Tahir, son of Imam al-Baqir (a.s.)
buried.note: A son of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) to whom a grave in the complex is attributed; it was moved here with Hudhayfah's in 1931.

tips: Stand at Salman's tomb facing the qiblah for [his ziyarat](AJ2), as it instructs.
Hudhayfah's tomb is in the second building of the complex, and the graves of Jabir and Tahir in the third.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/ (المرقد الشريف للصحابي سلمان الفارسي, مزار الصحابي حذيفة بن اليمان)

sites.name: Taq Kasra (Arch of Ctesiphon)
sites.about: The great brick arch of the Sasanian palace at Ctesiphon, a short walk south of Salman's shrine. Imam Ali (a.s.) prayed there by narration, and Mafatih al-Jinan recommends praying at the site in his memory and reflecting on the passing of earthly power.
tips: Pray two rak'ats here as Imam Ali (a.s.) did; the corpus does not yet hold Mafatih's section on it.

cities.name: Mashhad
cities.about: Mashhad, in north-eastern Iran, grew up around the grave of Imam Ali al-Reza (a.s.), the eighth Imam, who was martyred in Tus in 203 AH; its name means "the place of martyrdom". He is the only one of the Twelve Imams buried in Iran, and pilgrims call him Gharib al-Ghuraba, the stranger far from home. The shrine complex at the city's centre, with the Goharshad Mosque inside it, is visited by millions every year.
tips: Most pilgrims stay within walking distance of the shrine; the streets around it are closed to traffic, and its courtyards are open day and night.
The shrine is most crowded on his birth (11 Dhul Qa'dah) and martyrdom (end of Safar), when many walk to Mashhad from other cities, and on 23 Dhul Qa'dah, a recommended day for his ziyarat.

Bags, phones and cameras are checked at the gates and large bags are left at the cloakrooms, so carry only what you need. Women wear the chador inside the haram; one can usually be borrowed at the entrance.

Ziyarat by a pilgrim who knows the Imam's right carries great reward by narration: he promised to come to his visitors at three hard moments - when the books of deeds fly, at the Sirat, and at the Scale.
Before you leave, recite the farewell at the tomb, as the Imams taught for every shrine.

sites.name: Shrine of Imam Ali al-Reza (a.s.)
sites.about: The tomb of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Reza (a.s.), the eighth Imam, who was summoned to Khurasan by the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun, named his heir, and martyred by poison in 203 AH. The golden-domed tomb chamber stands at the heart of a complex of porticoes (riwaqs) and courtyards that has grown over more than a thousand years. Imam al-Jawad (a.s.) taught the ziyarat known as al-Jawadiyya for his father, and by narration a visit to him is counted among the greatest of acts.

ziyarat.label: First Ziyarat of Imam Reza (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: The best-known ziyarat, from Shaykh al-Saduq.
Especially on 23 Dhul Qa'dah, his birth (11 Dhul Qa'dah) and his martyrdom (end of Safar).
On Wednesdays, the day of the four Imams from Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) to Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.).
Can be recited at the shrine of any of the Imams (a.s.).

ziyarat.label: Farewell to Imam Reza (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: When leaving the shrine.
After the ziyarat.

buried.name: Shaykh Baha'i (Baha al-Din al-Amili)
buried.note: Jurist, mathematician and author of Miftah al-Falah; he died in Isfahan and was brought to Mashhad by his will. His tomb is in the portico named after him, where he used to teach.

buried.name: Shaykh al-Hurr al-Amili
buried.note: Muhaddith from Jabal Amil and compiler of Wasa'il al-Shi'a; he settled in Mashhad and was buried in the shrine complex.

buried.name: Amin al-Islam al-Tabarsi
buried.note: Author of the Quran commentary Majma' al-Bayan. His tomb is shown on the north side of the complex, though some place his grave elsewhere.

tips: Ask permission to enter at the door of the haram, then go to the tomb; after the ziyarat pray two units of ziyarat prayer at the head side.
Men and women enter the tomb chamber from separate sides, and the crowd around the zarih is often very heavy; the ziyarat can be recited from the porticoes as well.
The drums of the Naqqarah Khanah are played over the old courtyard at sunrise and sunset, a centuries-old custom of the shrine.
Large congregational prayers are held in the Goharshad Mosque, on the south side of the tomb.

sites.name: Goharshad Mosque
sites.about: The great congregational mosque of the shrine, on the south side of the tomb of Imam al-Reza (a.s.), reached through the Dar al-Siyadah portico. It was built from 821 AH (1418 CE) by Goharshad, wife of the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh, to the design of Qavam al-Din Shirazi, with four iwans, a turquoise dome and two minarets.
tips: The shrine's daily congregational prayers are held here.
Many pilgrims pray here before or after going to the tomb, as it lies right beside the tomb chamber.

sites.name: Tomb of Khwaja Rabi'
sites.about: The tomb of al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, one of the early Tabi'in and a companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), about 6 km north of the shrine of Imam al-Reza (a.s.). The domed mausoleum standing today was built by order of Shah Abbas I, on the advice of Shaykh Baha'i, and finished in 1617 CE; tradition holds that Imam al-Reza (a.s.) visited the grave.

ziyarat.label: At the grave of a believer

buried.name: Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym (Khwaja Rabi')
buried.note: An early Tabi'i known for his asceticism and a companion of Imam Ali (a.s.); buried under the dome.

tips: It is a short drive from the shrine; many pilgrims visit it on the same day as the other sites around Mashhad.
The garden around the mausoleum is also a cemetery, with many martyrs and believers buried there.

ziyarat.label: First Ziyarat of Imam Reza (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: The best-known ziyarat, from Shaykh al-Saduq.

ziyarat.label: Farewell to Imam Reza (a.s.)
ziyarat.note: When leaving the shrine.

features.name: Sahn Azadi
